belongs_to: 'Continue the pattern given below and colour it appropriately.' (start of the pattern drawn on dotted triangular grid)
description: A blue dashed rounded rectangle (landscape) filled with an isometric (triangular) dot lattice: 16 rows of dots, rows alternately offset by half a spacing, 30 dots in the odd rows and 29 in the even rows (counted by pixel analysis), the first row 30. The start of the pattern sits at the top-left, drawn with thin red outlines: 3 regular hexagons filled PURPLE and 10 equilateral triangles filled YELLOW-ORANGE (pale orange). Every hexagon side and every triangle side is 2 dot spacings long. Layout (hexagon H1 left, H2 right, H3 below between them): H1 and H2 sit side by side at the top with one down-pointing triangle above and one up-pointing triangle below their shared vertex (so 2 hexagons and 2 triangles meet there alternately); H3 sits below and between them, its top edge being the base of that lower up-pointing triangle. The 10 yellow triangles, band by band from the top: band 1: 2 up-pointing triangles, one on top of H1 and one on top of H2; band 2: 3 down-pointing triangles (left of H1's top, between H1 and H2, right of H2's top); band 3: 2 up-pointing triangles (below-left of H1, and the one between H1, H2 and H3); band 4: 1 down-pointing triangle (below H1, left of H3); band 5: 1 up-pointing triangle (lower-left of H3); band 6: 1 down-pointing triangle (below H3). Every placed hexagon is therefore surrounded by alternating triangles and hexagons as in P04-pattern-1. Still empty: the down-pointing triangle slot at the right of the H2/H3 junction, and everything to the right of and below the cluster. The rest of the lattice is blank.

belongs_to: 'Here is a tiling pattern made using two different shapes - squares and triangles. Are the triangles equilateral? Why or why not? What shapes are coming together at the marked points? Are the same set of shapes coming together at these points? Continue the pattern and colour it appropriately.'
description: A red dashed rounded rectangle (landscape) with square dot paper (45 dots across, 16 dots down; counted by pixel analysis). At the top-left a small cluster of 3 SQUARES (filled lilac, tilted, not aligned to the grid) and 2 TRIANGLES (filled orange), thin blue outlines, 5 RED dots on vertices. In dot spacings d: each square has side sqrt(5) d (a step of 2 across and 1 down); each triangle is isosceles with base 2d and the other two sides sqrt(5) d, so the triangles are NOT equilateral (base slightly shorter than the other sides; base angles about 63 degrees, apex angle about 53 degrees). Name the red dots A (left end of T1's vertical side, upper), B (lower end of that side), C (T1's apex, to the right), D (top apex of T2), E (T2's lower-right vertex). T1 = triangle A-B-C: a vertical side AB of length 2d on the left and its apex C to the right. T2 = triangle C-D-E: horizontal base CE of length 2d at the bottom and its apex D above. Square S1 (top-left) has the side A-C in common with T1 and the side C-D in common with T2. Square S2 (right) has the side D-E in common with T2. Square S3 (below) has the side B-C in common with T1. So around point C the shapes are S1, T2, S3 and T1 in that order with a gap of about 63 degrees (the size of a triangle's base angle) between T2 and S3, still to be filled. The rest of the dot paper is empty.
unclear: Side lengths in dot units (2d and sqrt(5) d) are measured from the picture; red dots read as 5.

belongs_to: Play with Circles '(a) Draw a circle with a compass and mark its centre. (b) Draw its diameter... (c) Draw another diameter... (d) Now join the four points. What shape is formed?'
description: A circle filled blue with a thin dark outline. Its centre is marked with a black dot. Two diameters are drawn as black dashed lines through the centre: one nearly horizontal (left end at the left edge, slightly lower than the right end) and one steeply slanted from the upper right to the lower left. The 4 endpoints of the diameters on the circle are marked with black dots (4 endpoints + the centre dot = 5 black dots; counted). The four endpoints are joined by 4 black dashed lines forming a tilted rectangle (opposite sides parallel and equal) inscribed in the circle, its vertices exactly on the circle and its diagonals the two diameters. No letters or numbers.

belongs_to: Circle Designs 'Look at the circle given below. It is marked with points 1 to 24. Join points 1 to 11, 11 to 2, 2 to 12, and so on till you reach back at 1.' - Step 1, Step 2, Step 3 (three circles side by side)
description: Three identical circles printed side by side, each with the heading badge 'Step 1' (pink), 'Step 2' (purple), 'Step 3' (blue) above it. Each circle is a thin dark dashed circle with 24 equally spaced points (small black-ringed pale-peach dots), numbered 1 to 24 clockwise outside the circle with the numbers rotated to follow the circle: 1 at the top (just left of the vertical), 2 just right of the top, 7 at the right (3 o'clock), 13 at the bottom, 19 at the left. Step 1: two dashed lines: a pink line from point 1 to point 11 and a blue line from point 2 to point 11. Step 2: the same two lines plus a green dashed line from point 2 to point 12 (a vertical line, since 2 and 12 are opposite). Step 3: the same three lines plus an orange dashed line from point 12 to point 3 (so far: pink 1-11, blue 11-2, green 2-12, orange 12-3). The remaining joins are not drawn.

belongs_to: Circle Designs 'Can you think of a way to make a design exactly like the image given here? Try to make it.'

Regions: 4 yellow lens-shapes, one at each of the four outer tips (top, bottom, left, right; each is the part of an outer circle farthest from the centre, bounded by that circle's outer arc and a second arc of the same radius curving towards the centre); 8 green curved-triangle pieces, two flanking each yellow lens (counted: the remaining outer part of each outer circle); 4 small purple curved triangles, one at each diagonal (corner) of the central circle where two neighbouring outer circles cross its edge; in the middle, 4 petal-shaped blue lenses (the four overlaps of neighbouring outer circles inside the central circle) meeting at the centre point like a four-leaf clover, and 4 pale yellow-green regions between the petals at the top, bottom, left and right inside the central circle. Black outlines on all arcs.
unclear: The yellow lenses' inner boundary is a same-size arc centred on the outermost point of each outer circle; it was fitted by overlaying circles on the picture, not stated in the book.

belongs_to: Cube Connections 1 'Here are three views of a cube. Can you draw them on the net in the correct order?'
description: A yellow square panel holding three isometric pictures of a cube (each shows the top face and two side faces, left and right). View 1 (top left): top face purple with a green square in its middle; left face light blue with an orange circle; right face pale yellow with a red/coral plus-shaped cross (a vertical and a horizontal line with a dot at each of the 4 ends). View 2 (top right): top face purple with a green square; left face pale yellow with the red cross; right face pink with a light-cyan (turquoise) 5-pointed star. View 3 (below view 1, bottom left): top face dark brown (maroon, plain); left face light blue with the orange circle; right face pale yellow with the red cross. So the six faces of the cube are: purple with green square, brown, light blue with orange circle, pale yellow with red cross, pink with cyan star, and a sixth (the bottom) not visible in any view.
unclear: The sixth face is not visible in any of the three views.

belongs_to: 'Which shapes did you make?' (straw and clay models) - first model (left, blue balls)
description: A skeleton model made of blue clay balls joined by pale-tan straws: 6 balls and 12 straws (counted): one ball at the top, one at the bottom and four balls around the middle (left, right, one at the back that is smaller, one at the front); each of the top and bottom balls is joined by a straw to each of the 4 middle balls (8 straws) and the four middle balls are joined in a ring of 4 straws. This is an octahedron skeleton (8 triangular faces).

belongs_to: 'Which shapes did you make?' (straw and clay models) - second model (middle, green balls)
description: A skeleton model made of green clay balls joined by pale-yellow straws: 6 balls and 9 straws (counted). One ball at the apex at the top, two balls at the middle left and right (joined to each other by a horizontal straw and each joined to the apex), one larger ball at the centre front (joined to the apex by a thick straw), two balls at the bottom left and right (joined to each other by a horizontal straw, and each also joined to the centre-front ball); each middle-side ball is joined by a straw down to the bottom ball on the same side. So two triangles (the top one: apex + the two middle balls; the front one: centre-front ball + two bottom balls) joined by 3 straws: a triangular prism skeleton.
